content: 1. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of quinine by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism and also by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 4. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of rasagiline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when combined with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 5. Regorafenib increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by likely inhibiting the BCRP (ABCG2) transporter. Co-administration with a BCRP substrate may increase systemic exposure and related toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 6. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This interaction may lead to treatment failure or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by dual inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2, potentially increasing systemic exposure and adverse reactions. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 9. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ropinirole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 10. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 11. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib and ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 12. Safinamide increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor BCRP substrates for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 13. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates and consider dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 14. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 15. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms and extended-release formulations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 17. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility (practically insoluble at pH > 5). Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the BCRP transporter. Co-administration may increase systemic exposure of BCRP substrates. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 19. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, limit use to less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 20. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and the BCRP transporter. Consider dosage reduction for BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 22. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 23. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 25. Tafamidis and tafamidis meglumine increase the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the BCRP transporter, potentially increasing exposure of BCRP substrates. Dosage adjustment of these substrates may be necessary. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 26. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 27. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by decreasing renal clearance and inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 28. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 29. Cimetidine and tenofovir DF increase each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 30. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tetanus toxoid (adsorbed or fluid) by decreasing metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 31. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 32. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of timolol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 33. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 34. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Decrease the dose of tofacitinib if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 35. Cimetidine decreases the effects of tramadol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 36. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 37. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of triamterene by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 38. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 39. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 40. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by increasing exposure of BCRP substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects and reduce substrate doses as needed. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 41. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of valacyclovir by decreasing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 42. Vandetanib increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the uptake of organic cation transporter type 2 (OCT2) substrates. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 44. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of verapamil by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 45. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, and vinorelbine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 46. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of vismodegib by increasing gastric pH, which alters its solubility and reduces bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 47. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 48. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 49. Cimetidine increases the levels of zolmitriptan by an unknown mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 51. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 52. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 53. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 54. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of amphetamine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 55. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of antipyrine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 56. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 57. Armodafinil increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 58. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of asenapine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 59. Blessed thistle decreases the effects of cimetidine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and the clinical significance is minor or unknown. 60. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 61. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 62. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 63. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of caffeine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 64. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of celecoxib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 65. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of chlorpromazine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 66. Cimetidine decreases the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 67. Devil's claw decreases the effects of cimetidine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 68. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 69. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 70. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of diclofenac by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 71. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH and by competing with basic (cationic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 72. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of donepezil by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 73. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 74. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting hepatic enzymes CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 75. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of encainide by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 76. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 77. Cimetidine and famciclovir interact through aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition, potentially affecting the conversion of 6-deoxy penciclovir to penciclovir. The clinical significance is minor or unknown.
